L2-optimal wavelet splatting is a volume rendering technique that projects volume data by accumulating scaled and translated wavelet basis functions (splats) onto a multiresolution grid [S1, unofficial][S2][S3, unofficial].

The claim states that L2-optimal wavelet splatting is a volume rendering technique that projects volume data by accumulating scaled and translated wavelet basis functions (splats) onto a multiresolution grid. It states that splats are approximated on a 'multiresolution grid' and that the rendering involves a linear combination (accumulation) of wavelet splats (scaled and translated basis functions). Source [S3] corroborates this, stating the method decomposes data into a wavelet pyramid, computes splats via least squares, and projects them onto a multiresolution grid. The mathematical formulation in [S1] also supports the accumulation of scaled and translated wavelet basis functions. Therefore, all facts in the claim are supported by the evidence.
